summary: EASD 2026 (Milan, 29 Sep–2 Oct) produced most of today's GLP-1 news, and much of it is fresh, published or presented work. Mainstream news has picked it up in the last 24–36 hours, but YouTube explainers haven't yet. The best openings are headline decoders that name a drug people know, which matches our playbook. 1) EloraTZP (the eloralintide + tirzepatide combo) lost up to 23.3% vs 14.8% on tirzepatide 15 mg at 48 weeks in a 367-person phase 2b in T2D. The story is in Reuters, STAT, WSJ and CNBC, and almost nobody has explained it for consumers yet. 2) People who switched from GLP-1 injections to the Wegovy pill lost another 4.1% in 3 months (OCTANE, real-world). This answers a search question many people already have: "can I switch to the pill?" 3) Orforglipron's ACHIEVE-4 (Lancet) showed cardiovascular safety vs insulin glargine. 4) A first controlled study found nail detachment in 39% of GLP-1 users vs 9% of controls (EADV), a new side-effect search term. 5) Trevogrumab roughly halved lean-mass loss on semaglutide (COURAGE, n=975), which fits the muscle pillar. Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 is now peaking: it's published in the Lancet and covered by every outlet, so only a 'decode the 50 lb / 30% headlines' angle is worth doing. The semaglutide 2 mg vs tirzepatide switch MACE data is industry-funded claims data and sits next to switching advice, so it's marked caution. Paediatric GLP-1 topics fall outside our adult audience. The NAION lawsuits are peaking and fear-driven, so we'd only cover them as a calm risk explainer, which we already made.

candidates.topic: EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide) vs tirzepatide 15 mg: up to 23.3% vs 14.8% weight loss at 48 weeks in adults with obesity/overweight and type 2 diabetes (phase 2b, 367 adults, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Did Lilly's new combo really beat Mounjaro?' Explain amylin (a second fullness hormone) added to tirzepatide. Give the numbers with arms: 23.3% is the top dose, the range across doses was 13.2–23.3%, and eloralintide alone gave 8.2–12.3%. Cover the population (T2D), the phase 2 caveat, more GI side effects and dropouts, Phase 3 planned by end of 2026, and that it isn't approved. Close with what this means for people on tirzepatide today: nothing changes, talk to your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Presented and press-released 30 Sep with Reuters, STAT, WSJ, CNBC, MarketWatch and Fierce coverage within hours. The brand-new name 'EloraTZP' has almost no consumer explainers on YouTube yet, and it fits the 'Did X really beat Y?' format that beats our median.

evidence.signal: Up to 23.3% weight loss and 2.9% A1C drop vs 14.8%/2.4% with tirzepatide 15 mg at 48 weeks
367 adults in a 48-week phase 2b; dose range 13.2–23.3%; eloralintide monotherapy 8.2–12.3%
Mainstream pickup on 30 Sep
Eloralintide program registry

candidates.topic: Switching from GLP-1 injections to the Wegovy pill (oral semaglutide 25 mg): average 4.1% further weight loss at 3 months (OCTANE real-world, Ro telehealth data, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Search-style question: 'Does the Wegovy pill work if you switch from the shot?' Answer: in this real-world cohort, on average people kept losing, 4.1% (4.0 kg) at 3 months, and 40.7% lost 5% or more. Caveats: retrospective, Novo-funded, only 3 months, switchers from both semaglutide and tirzepatide, no comparison group. Also cover pill basics (empty stomach, a small sip of water, wait before eating, as labelled) without dosing. Any switch is a decision for your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Reuters and CNBC carried it on 30 Sep, the Wegovy pill launched in 2026, and 'does the Wegovy pill really work' already shows up as a query signal. Many viewers are weighing a shot vs a pill right now.

evidence.signal: 4.1% (4.0 kg) mean weight loss at 3 months after switching
Retrospective Ro cohort; switched Jan–Feb 2026 from injectable semaglutide or tirzepatide; 40.7% reached ≥5%
Trade coverage

candidates.topic: GLP-1 users and nail detachment: 39% vs 9% in comparable non-users, the first controlled study (575 users vs 1,329 controls, EADV 2026)
candidates.angle: Side-effect explainer people will search: 'Can Ozempic affect your nails?' What onycholysis is, the numbers (39% vs 9% detachment, 46% vs 17% discoloration), and that the difference held even among people who lost weight. Caveats: congress abstract, cross-sectional and self-reported, not yet peer-reviewed. Friendly nail-care and nutrition habits (protein, an overall varied diet), and when to see a GP or dermatologist. Pair it with our hair-loss piece as a 'hair, skin and nails on GLP-1' series.
candidates.why_now: Medical Xpress on 30 Sep, then fast syndication (Mirage, Bioengineer). Nail complaints already circulate on Reddit and TikTok, and now a controlled number exists. Creators haven't picked it up yet.

evidence.signal: 39% of GLP-1 users reported nail detachment vs 9% of controls; first controlled study
575 users vs 1,329 controls across France, US, Brazil and Mexico; EADV 2026

candidates.topic: Trevogrumab (anti-myostatin) + semaglutide cut lean-mass loss by about half: 3.3% vs 6.7% at 26 weeks (Regeneron COURAGE phase 2, 975 adults, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: The muscle question everyone on a GLP-1 asks. Explain what share of weight lost is lean mass on semaglutide, what myostatin is, and the COURAGE numbers with arms and timeframe. It's experimental and not approved, with side effects to note. Then pivot to what works now: protein (unless your clinician has told you to limit it), resistance training, and pacing. Keeps the 'muscle vs fat' pillar fresh with a real hook.
keywords: how to keep muscle on Ozempic
candidates.why_now: Reuters 'halves muscle loss' headline on 30 Sep, plus a Yahoo doctor piece on Ozempic muscle loss and a new Clin Nutr paper on creatine for GLP-1 muscle loss. Several independent sources point to the same question.

evidence.signal: Lean-mass loss 3.3% with trevogrumab 75 mg + semaglutide vs 6.7% with semaglutide alone at 26 weeks
Lean mass preserved during and after semaglutide-induced weight loss
Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss (commentary)

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) pill passes its heart-safety test vs insulin glargine in type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4, Lancet, 2,700+ adults)
candidates.angle: Decoder: 'Is the new GLP-1 pill safe for your heart?' Non-inferior for MACE (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.59–1.20). It was not designed to show superiority. The all-cause death signal (HR 0.43) is nominal and needs caution. It's open-label vs insulin, in T2D at increased CV risk. Plus the A1C and weight changes. Builds on our orforglipron series.
candidates.why_now: Published in the Lancet on 30 Sep with MedPage, Medical Xpress and Lilly coverage. It hasn't reached consumers yet, Foundayo is a newly launched brand name people are searching, and our orforglipron long-form had the top views.

evidence.signal: MACE HR 0.84 (0.59–1.20), non-inferiority met; all-cause mortality HR 0.43 nominal
ACHIEVE-4 primary publication
Primary source

candidates.topic: Petrelintide, an amylin-only shot: up to 10.7% weight loss (vs 1.7% placebo) at 42 weeks with only 1.5% stopping for GI side effects (ZUPREME-1, Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology)
candidates.angle: 'Is there a weight-loss shot with less nausea?' Explain amylin vs GLP-1 in plain words. Give the numbers with placebo context and the top dose, plus the gentler GI profile in phase 2. It's not approved, and the weight loss is smaller than GLP-1s. Explains the amylin wave (CagriSema, EloraTZP, petrelintide) as one family.
candidates.why_now: Lancet D&E publication on 29 Sep, a Medical Xpress 'alternative to GLP-1' story and Healio on 30 Sep. Amylin is becoming a theme across three EASD readouts.

evidence.signal: 10% weight loss with adverse events comparable to placebo
ZUPREME 1 phase 2 publication
10.7% top dose; 1.5% GI discontinuation

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 in the Lancet: decoding the '50 pounds', '60 pounds' and '30% like surgery' headlines (up to 20.8% vs 4.0% placebo at 80 weeks in T2D with obesity)
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Did retatrutide really match weight-loss surgery?' Sort the headlines out: USA Today's 50 lb, NBC's 'up to 60 lb', the Business Journals' 30% (a different trial and population) and Pharmacy Times' 18.8% (a different estimand). Show which number belongs to which trial, population and estimand. It's not approved, and FDA timing should be hedged.
candidates.why_now: Published 29 Sep and covered by every major outlet with conflicting numbers. Demand is huge but so is competition; the differentiated angle is the confusion between numbers.

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2 phase 3 publication
'Average weight loss of 50 pounds' headline
'New high-water mark' framing

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Zepbound) vs high-dose semaglutide 7.2 mg (Wegovy HD): Lilly's indirect comparison says 3.2–4.5 points more weight loss at 72 weeks
candidates.angle: 'Did Zepbound really beat Wegovy HD?' Explain what an indirect treatment comparison is (SURMOUNT-1 vs STEP UP, different trials, not head-to-head) and that it's company-sponsored. Note no head-to-head vs 7.2 mg has been found as of Sept 2026, and that both work well. Verify the absolute figures against the primary release before scripting: secondary reports give 20.2% vs 13.7%, which conflicts with published STEP UP results.
keywords: which works better Zepbound or Wegovy
candidates.why_now: Lilly and Novo are in an EASD data war: indirect comparisons, orforglipron vs oral semaglutide, and Novo's MACE claims. 'Zepbound vs Wegovy' is a top evergreen search, freshly refreshed by Wegovy HD.

evidence.signal: Indirect treatment comparison, tirzepatide 10/15 mg vs semaglutide 7.2 mg
Lilly building its commercial case with indirect analyses
Independent indirect comparison of tirzepatide vs semaglutide in people without T2D

candidates.topic: Cost and sticking with it: GLP-1 non-adherence rose above 80% once monthly out-of-pocket costs passed $75 (UGA, JAMA Health Forum, 8,914 insured adults)
candidates.angle: Life-on-GLP-1 explainer: why people stop and why it matters (link to our 'stopping' content: weight regain and heart data). Numbers: a $75 tipping point, and even in the cheapest tier about 3 in 4 stopped within a year. Practical, legitimate options: ask about coverage, appeals, manufacturer savings programs and Medicare's cap. Never compounded or gray-market sources.
candidates.why_now: UGA, Fox 5, Futurity and Medical Xpress on 30 Sep, plus the Boston Globe on coverage shifts and equity. It ties into our rising 'stopping GLP-1 risk' topic, seen 5 times.

evidence.signal: 8,914 patients; non-adherence >80% above $75/month
Mainstream pickup

candidates.topic: Why some people lose 20% on semaglutide and others barely lose: predictors of peak weight loss in SELECT (Diabetes Care) plus the 'non-responder' question
candidates.angle: Answer a question the audience asks emotionally ('Is something wrong with me?'). Cover what predicted bigger loss in SELECT (adults with established CVD plus overweight/obesity), what trials show on responder rates, and that heart benefit in SELECT wasn't mainly explained by weight. Encouraging message: talk to your prescriber about your plan, and weight is one measure among many.
keywords: why am I not losing weight on Ozempic
candidates.why_now: A Yahoo doctor explainer published today plus the 24 Sep Diabetes Care SELECT predictors paper. Fits our evergreen non-responder topic with a fresh hook.

evidence.signal: Predictors of peak body weight loss with semaglutide in SELECT
'Some lose 20%, others barely any' explainer

candidates.topic: Does Ozempic curb alcohol cravings? Semaglutide trials in alcohol use disorder (JAMA Psychiatry RCT; oral semaglutide 8-week trial, CU Anschutz 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Does Ozempic make you want to drink less?' What small RCTs show: fewer heavy-drinking days and lower craving vs placebo. Explain the brain reward-system mechanism. Caveats: small and short trials, not approved for AUD, and people should get help through proper channels. Pairs with today's PsyPost mouse reward-seeking study, labelled 'in mice'.
candidates.why_now: ScienceAlert on 30 Sep plus PsyPost's semaglutide reward-seeking mouse study. Interest in 'Dry January' prep starts building in Q4.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide reduced heavy drinking and craving in AUD (JAMA Psychiatry RCT)
Oral semaglutide 8-week AUD trial

candidates.topic: Ozempic 2 mg vs switching to Mounjaro and heart risk: decoding Novo's '6% lower MACE' real-world claim (COMPETE SWITCH CV, 208,000+ adults with T2D, claims data)
candidates.angle: Headline decoder that teaches evidence literacy: an adjusted HR of 1.06 for the switch group is a small relative difference. It's company-funded retrospective claims data with very unequal groups (185,705 vs 23,104), and it isn't proof that either choice is better. Explicitly no switching advice: decisions belong with your prescriber. Pair with Lilly's indirect comparisons as 'the EASD marketing war, explained'.
candidates.why_now: Novo PR on 29 Sep and HCPLive, Cardiovascular Business and Benzinga coverage. 'Should I switch to Mounjaro?' is a common query, but the topic risks reading as switching advice.

evidence.signal: aHR 1.06 (1.04–1.08) for MACE with tirzepatide switch vs semaglutide 2 mg escalation
Primary press release

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and stroke in people with atrial fibrillation and type 2 diabetes vs GLP-1 RAs (Nature Communications), plus SURPASS-CVOT signals on infection mortality
candidates.angle: Benefits beyond weight, with exact populations. Tirzepatide vs other GLP-1 RAs in AFib plus T2D (observational, so 'linked to'). The SURPASS-CVOT secondary findings are exploratory. Keep wording at the evidence level and name the comparator explicitly.
candidates.why_now: Nat Commun paper plus Medscape SURPASS-CVOT coverage on 30 Sep, and tirzepatide linked to lower diabetic eye disease risk (Medical Economics). There's a cluster of tirzepatide benefit-beyond-weight data.

evidence.signal: Tirzepatide vs GLP-1 RAs and stroke in AF + T2D
SURPASS-CVOT: infection mortality and patient-reported outcomes signals

candidates.topic: GLP-1 tummy side effects across today's and tomorrow's drugs: a new expert review of nausea, constipation and vomiting for injectables, pills and pipeline agents (Nutrition in Clinical Practice, Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: How-to: making common GI side effects easier. Cover how often they happen, why (slower stomach emptying), and evidence-based habits: smaller meals, eating slowly, stopping at full, fibre and fluids (unless you've been told to limit fluids), and avoiding very fatty meals. Red flags: severe tummy pain spreading to the back means 911/999 or the ER/A&E. Fresh hook: the pills (orforglipron, Wegovy pill) and amylin drugs compared.
keywords: how to stop nausea on Ozempic
candidates.why_now: New October review plus a wave of new pills and combos where side effects are the main news caveat (EloraTZP's higher dropouts, petrelintide's placebo-like GI). High evergreen search demand.

evidence.signal: Narrative expert review of GI adverse effects of approved, oral and pipeline GLP-1/GIP agents
More side effects with the Zepbound combo, a consumer angle

candidates.topic: Women are the main GLP-1 users, but research gaps remain (pregnancy, menopause, periods): new review plus the French nationwide pregnancy safety study (Diabetologia)
candidates.angle: Women-focused explainer extending our menopause and orforglipron content. What's known (menopause post-hocs), what isn't, and the pregnancy data (observational, T2D). Clear message: talk to your clinician if planning pregnancy. No advice to stop on your own.
candidates.why_now: Medical Xpress on 30 Sep plus a Diabetologia pregnancy safety paper on 29 Sep. Our menopause long-form was the top performer.

evidence.signal: Women are the predominant GLP-1 users; research gaps
French nationwide study on GLP-1 RA safety in pregnancy with T2D

candidates.topic: Children and teens on GLP-1s: 16.8% diagnosed with a nutritional deficiency within a year, mostly vitamin D (Childhood Obesity, Lurie Children's)
candidates.angle: Only as an adult-relevant lesson: 'Eating less means nutrients matter more.' Cover the counselling gap (5% got nutrition counselling within 30 days) and what adults can ask their clinician about. This is outside our core adult audience and its paediatric framing is sensitive, so it's lower priority.
candidates.why_now: SciTechDaily, Scripps and Northwestern coverage this week, plus ABC30 on rising paediatric use.
